transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Sophie Patel (Aurora Tech - Head of MLOps), Ravi Singh (Aurora Tech - CTO), Elena Park (Aurora Tech - Infra)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. will keep this to about 45 minutes for the walkthrough, leave time for q and a. i'm maya, ae for redwood. liam our se will do the console walk.
[00:24] Liam Ortega: hi all, yep, quick agenda: demo the usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, show how to map routes to models and routing policies, and then talk about dedicated vs hosted for your latency requirements.
[01:10] Sophie Patel: great, quick context — we run a multi-tenant chat assistant across consumer app and backend support workflows. current stack: using OpenAI hosted for prototypes, moving to dedicated endpoints for production. main concerns are per-route cost attribution, burst handling, and SOC2/audit logs.
[02:05] Ravi Singh: timeline is Q2 pilot, then evaluate for broader rollout. need to know what kind of SLOs and cost predictability we get.
[03:12] Liam Ortega: understood. i'll start in the console. one note: some of my labels might read redwood-internal things — sorry the auto captions sometimes swap names.
[05:00] [Screen share sounds] Liam Ortega: here's the main usage page — shows tokens and request counts over time, you can split by model, route, team, or customer. on the left are filters — route name, model family, date range.
[06:10] Elena Park: can we map our api routes to these routes? like /chat/user vs /support?
[06:28] Liam Ortega: yep, routes are configurable in the config layer — you map your incoming paths and apply policies. we'll demo a sample mapping for your support flow.
[07:40] Liam Ortega: now watch the per-route dashboard for /support-agent — notice the latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), token costs per-response, and a cost per-route column which factors in model, tokens, and infra.
[09:05] Sophie Patel: that cost-per-route calc — is that per-token USD or includes infra overhead?
[09:20] Liam Ortega: good question — it includes model unit price (hosted per-token) plus an infra overhead estimate when on dedicated; we show both hosted unit costs and adjusted dedicated unit economics. you can toggle to view raw token cost vs full landed cost. the breakdown shows prefix caching savings and batching benefits.
[12:30] [Demo continues] Liam Ortega: here's an example where we enabled prefix KV cache on the support route — CPU/gpu utilization dropped and token cost per request dropped ~18% in this workload.
[15:00] Ravi Singh: how do you attribute shared model usage between routes? our assistant and summaries share the same model, we need split billing.
[15:20] Liam Ortega: the console supports per-route tagging and attribution. we recommend mapping client-facing endpoints to unique route ids; for shared model calls we surface sampling-based attribution and you can export raw logs to csv for exact accounting.
[18:40] Maya Chen: quick interjection — for enterprise customers we can also provide a per-route billing export that plugs into your finops tooling.
[19:50] Sophie Patel: excellent. about quotas — can we set per-route quotas for cost control?
[20:10] Liam Ortega: yes, quotas and alerts. you can set soft and hard quotas; soft will trigger alerts and block above threshold optionally. alerts tie into pager duty or slack.
[22:00] [Slight cross-talk] Elena Park: what about model fallbacks — if we hit capacity on a dedicated pool can it route to a cheaper variant?
[22:22] Liam Ortega: yes, smart routing policies allow fallback by latency/cost tiers; example: default to high-accuracy model on dedicated, fallback to a quantized variant on hosted in another region. the console shows expected unit cost and latency difference for each policy. the fallback rules can be per-route.
[25:00] Liam Ortega: switching to the cost breakdown view — this shows weighted cost per route over the month, tokens, batching efficiency, and savings estimate if you move to dedicated with configured batching and KV cache.
[27:15] Sophie Patel: can you show an example with our traffic profile?
[27:30] Liam Ortega: i loaded a sample from aurora earlier; see here — consumer-chat has many short, chatty requests, high p50 but low tokens; backend-support has fewer requests but big context windows which blow up tokens. the console suggests quantization for the support route or a mixed deployment: dedicated for support (predictable cost) and hosted for consumer chat.
[30:05] Ravi Singh: curious about burst handling. we have big spikes during new releases.
[30:30] Liam Ortega: Dedicated supports autoscaling bursts and reserved/min capacity with burst credits; for hosted we recommend routing policy with burst to hosted and configured concurrency limits. we can show burst model of costs — you'll see a step function in cost when you scale up GPUs.
[33:10] Sophie Patel: security — SOC2 and VPC — can you walk through the logs and audit trail?
[33:35] Liam Ortega: console has an audit logs tab — shows token-level operations for admin actions, model rollouts, policy changes. for private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM and logs can be pushed to your SIEM.
[35:00] Elena Park: any caveats around KV cache and PHI/PII? we have regulated data in some support transcripts.
[35:30] Liam Ortega: best practice is to keep any PII in your sidecar and use redwood's prefix cache in encrypted form or disable caching for those routes. we also support data retention policies and deletion workflows. we'll include our SOC2 and privacy docs.
[38:00] [Benchmark discussion] Liam Ortega: for the pilot we recommend a 2-week canary, run our benchmark harness using your sample prompts. we'll measure p50/p95 and per-route cost, and recommend model quantization profiles. expected timeline: 1 week setup + 2 weeks running.
[40:15] Sophie Patel: what about model versions — if we pin a model and later want to roll out a newer one how are regressions detected?
[40:30] Liam Ortega: console integrates with Redwood Optimize — you can run evals against golden prompt sets. it flags quality regressions and ties alerts to rollouts; you can do canary traffic splits directly in console (A/B).
[42:55] Ravi Singh: pricing — can you give a ballpark for our expected monthly spend?
[43:10] Maya Chen: based on the sample we loaded, with current traffic mix we estimate ~ $18k/month on hosted for both routes; if you move support to dedicated the estimate becomes ~$11k/month fixed + variable for bursts — we'll send detailed sheet. (note: numbers are sample-estimates)
[45:00] Sophie Patel: sounds promising. a couple product questions: is per-route throttling programmable in infra as code?
[45:20] Liam Ortega: yes, routes and policies are in declarative config (yaml) and we have a cli and api for infra-as-code. we'll share examples.
[47:10] Sophie Patel: ok, last security clarification: SSO/SAML for admin access and RBAC?
[47:30] Maya Chen: yes, SSO/SAML, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC scopes. enterprise plan includes tighter audit retention.
[49:00] [Recap] Maya Chen: to recap — action items: we'll send pricing + throughput estimate, liam will draft benchmark and dashboard screenshots, elena to share anonymized prompts. next meeting to kick off pilot tentatively 2026-03-10 pending deliverables.
[50:05] Ravi Singh: we also want the SOC2 and VPC docs.
[50:20] Maya Chen: noted — i'll attach.
[51:00] [Goodbyes] Sophie Patel: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[51:15] Liam Ortega: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-caption had a few swaps (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "redwood-internal" label), removed some repeated filler lines but kept natural interruptions and cross-talk.

Shared artifacts referenced: pricing-sheet (link to be sent), SOC2 + VPC deployment doc (link), sample dashboard screenshots (to be attached).

End of transcript.
